drafts.subject: 兼容性测试提议｜把 X2Strategy 六阶段产物接入可恢复工作流
drafts.body:
ALAGENT 团队您好，

X2Strategy 的 README 把论文到策略的过程明确拆成解析、提取、代码生成、验证、回测和诊断，并在歧义、修复和生成前保留 `needs_human_review` 与结构化 StrategySpec。这个设计已经比“论文直接生成代码”更可审计；我们想验证的不是交易收益，而是这条六阶段链在可恢复工作流里是否仍能保持同样清晰的产物与人工判断边界。项目依据：
https://github.com/ALAGENT-HKU/x2strategy

我们建议做一个很小的兼容性实验：固定一篇公开论文和合成行情数据，先跑原生 X2Strategy 基线，再把同一 Skill 作为 LazyMind 工作流执行；在 validation→backtest 之间注入一次可恢复失败。验收只看四件事：StrategySpec、生成代码和 metrics 是否逐阶段可追溯；未决问题是否在代码生成前停下；恢复后是否避免重跑已完成的解析/提取；会话、步骤与最终任务状态是否一致。

LazyMind 可提供开源实现与现有的 Skill→Workflow 实验记录：
https://github.com/LazyAGI/LazyMind
https://github.com/NicoYang1984/LazyMind/blob/fde2e68437caffa8dc6d706271dabc6073183938/examples/competitive-brief-skill2workflow/EVALUATION.md
现有记录只证明了一个受限路径：安装、转换和发布成功；首次自主运行停在 2/5，人工辅助后会话达到 5/5，但原外部任务仍为 failed，报告也有事实依据问题。它不证明 X2Strategy 已集成、所有审批都会被强制执行，也不证明质量或性能提升。

我负责 LazyMind 的生态兼容性外联，这是一封与项目直接相关的合作询问。上述 Example 来自公开贡献分支并仍处于草稿 PR 评审语境，不代表 ALAGENT 或任何上游项目背书。若这个问题对你们有价值，我下一步只发送一页测试矩阵，供你们决定是否值得共同复现；不需要生产数据、真实资金或共享凭据。

这个范围适合通过你们的项目合作渠道继续讨论吗？若不相关，简单回复不适合即可，我们不会继续跟进。

LazyMind 生态兼容性外联
lazymind_agent@163.com

drafts.subject: Would a bounded LazyMind compatibility test be useful for one multi-stage skill?
drafts.body:
Your repository now supports Codex and a broad set of research, finance, commercial, product, human-gate, and agent-harness skills. The contribution guide also asks people to check overlap and discuss uncertain ideas before building, so I am proposing a test plan here rather than opening a promotional issue or PR. Sources: https://github.com/alirezarezvani/claude-skills and https://github.com/alirezarezvani/claude-skills/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md.

Would it be useful to select one genuinely multi-stage skill—for example the RFP responder or one research-operations skill—and run a bounded compatibility comparison? The same public/synthetic input, model, tool permissions and skill commit would be used twice: once natively, and once after installing the Skill into a LazyMind workflow. We would compare only inspectable behavior: stage artifacts, explicit review questions, restart/resume after one injected failure, and whether unaffected stages remain unchanged. We would not claim that wrapping a Skill improves answer quality.

LazyMind is open source at https://github.com/LazyAGI/LazyMind. The only prior example we would use as a starting point is https://github.com/NicoYang1984/LazyMind/blob/fde2e68437caffa8dc6d706271dabc6073183938/examples/competitive-brief-skill2workflow/EVALUATION.md. That record includes negative results: autonomous execution stopped at 2/5, assisted recovery reached 5/5 at the session layer, and the originating external task still reported failure. It does not establish compatibility with this repository or reliable unattended execution.

I coordinate ecosystem compatibility outreach for LazyMind and am posting in that project capacity. There is no existing integration or endorsement. If maintainers are open to the question, the next step would be a one-page matrix for review before anyone runs code. Which single skill, if any, would make this experiment useful rather than duplicative?

drafts.subject: Compatibility proposal: AG2 MCPToolkit × LazyMind workflow state
drafts.body:
Hello AG2 partnerships team,

AG2's current docs describe two pieces that make a narrow interoperability test possible without inventing a new host adapter: `MCPToolkit` can consume a local or remote MCP server while keeping credentials inside the caller's infrastructure, and AG2 already has human-input, workflow-channel and write-ahead-log primitives. Your ecosystem page explicitly invites agent platforms and protocols to propose integrations: https://www.ag2.ai/ecosystem.

Would you be open to reviewing a fixed compatibility test? An AG2 agent would call LazyMind's existing MCP workflow surface for one synthetic research task, pause at one review question, inspect step and artifact state, then resume after an injected recoverable failure. The pass/fail checks would be: no production credentials or data leave either test environment; AG2's audit events and LazyMind's workflow state do not contradict each other; a retry does not duplicate the downstream action; and a failed external task is not reported as complete merely because the agent session ended. The relevant AG2 MCP behavior is documented at https://docs.ag2.ai/docs/user-guide/tools/mcp_servers/.

LazyMind can provide the open-source workflow surface and its existing bounded experiment record:
https://github.com/LazyAGI/LazyMind
https://github.com/NicoYang1984/LazyMind/blob/fde2e68437caffa8dc6d706271dabc6073183938/examples/competitive-brief-skill2workflow/EVALUATION.md
That record is deliberately not a success claim: the autonomous run stopped at 2/5 steps; assisted recovery reached 5/5 at the session layer while the original external task remained failed; and the artifact still had grounding issues. We have not tested AG2 compatibility, and this note does not claim a released integration, performance benefit, or AG2 endorsement.

I coordinate ecosystem compatibility outreach for LazyMind and am contacting you in that project capacity. If this is relevant to AG2's platform/protocol partnership track, the next step would be a one-page test matrix for maintainer review, using only public or synthetic inputs and no request for your production access. Would that be an appropriate scope?

LazyMind ecosystem outreach
lazymind_agent@163.com

drafts.subject: Design-partner test: running LazyMind's MCP workflow surface under ToolHive
drafts.body:
Hello Stacklok / ToolHive team,

Your ToolHive design-partner invitation is unusually specific: teams running MCP in real environments are asked to bring concrete infrastructure and governance problems, while the open-source project manages MCP servers and agent skills. The invitation and contact route are documented at https://stacklok.com/blog/increasing-the-toolhive-buzz-by-making-mcp-simpler-and-more-secure/ and https://stacklok.com/contact/.

We would like to propose a small public/synthetic test, not a production deployment claim. The test would register LazyMind's existing MCP workflow surface under ToolHive, restrict it to the minimum workflow/status/artifact tools, start one fixed task, and restart the MCP server during a recoverable step. We would check discovery and least-privilege configuration, whether workflow and artifact state remain truthful after restart, whether a human-review stop can be resumed without duplicating completed work, and whether ToolHive and LazyMind logs agree about success versus failure. No customer data, production credentials, or unrelated servers would be involved.

LazyMind is open source at https://github.com/LazyAGI/LazyMind. Its only existing evidence for this outreach is the bounded Skill-to-Workflow example at https://github.com/NicoYang1984/LazyMind/blob/fde2e68437caffa8dc6d706271dabc6073183938/examples/competitive-brief-skill2workflow/EVALUATION.md. That run included failures: autonomous execution stopped at 2/5; assisted recovery reached 5/5 at the session layer while the originating task remained failed. It does not establish a ToolHive package, production compatibility, universal recovery, or mandatory approval enforcement.

I coordinate ecosystem compatibility outreach for LazyMind and am writing in that project capacity. If this fits the design-partner route, the next step would only be a one-page matrix and proposed local setup for your review. Would your team consider that useful, or is the invitation limited to teams already operating ToolHive in production?

LazyMind ecosystem outreach
lazymind_agent@163.com

drafts.subject: Partnership test: one authenticated Composio action inside an observable LazyMind workflow
drafts.body:
Hello Composio partnerships team,

Your partnership page asks agent platforms and developer platforms to propose a concrete user journey, and it explicitly includes integrations, starter kits and reference architectures: https://composio.dev/partnerships. A narrow shared question is what should happen when a long-running workflow reaches an authenticated external action, then encounters a recoverable failure before the overall task is complete.

We propose one test-account journey: a LazyMind workflow prepares a synthetic record, reaches an explicit review checkpoint, performs one reversible Composio-authenticated action, stores the action receipt as an artifact, and then replays the recovery path. The acceptance checks would be that auth remains on the Composio side, the workflow never treats a pending/failed external action as completion, and retry logic cannot create the action twice. This would be a compatibility experiment only; any integration, reference architecture or co-marketing discussion would depend on the result and a separate review.

LazyMind can provide its open-source workflow surface and the existing bounded experiment record:
https://github.com/LazyAGI/LazyMind
https://github.com/NicoYang1984/LazyMind/blob/fde2e68437caffa8dc6d706271dabc6073183938/examples/competitive-brief-skill2workflow/EVALUATION.md
The prior run is not a success or performance claim: autonomous execution stopped at 2/5; assisted recovery reached 5/5 at the session layer while the original external task remained failed; and the report still had grounding problems. We have not tested Composio compatibility, enforced approval, or duplicate-safe action recovery.

I coordinate ecosystem compatibility outreach for LazyMind and am contacting you in that project capacity. The linked example was contributed through a public fork and remains in a draft-PR review context; there is no existing Composio integration or endorsement. If this user journey fits your partnership intake, the next step would be a one-page test matrix using only a dedicated test account and reversible data. Would that be appropriate?

LazyMind ecosystem outreach
lazymind_agent@163.com
